title: Job record
description: One target, one file, one writer: jobs/<id>.json. Every enum here used to be a comment in a SQL schema, which is how a channel column ended up holding a sentence. Descriptive text belongs in notes, evidence, incidents or escalations. Human pipeline state (stage, priority, salary expectation, human notes) is NOT here: it lives in career.db, where a rebuild never touches it.

id.description: <company>-<role-slug>[-<n>]. Deliberately NOT equal to company_id: re-applying to a company next year is normal, and one-per-company is a gate policy, not a primary key.

domains.description: Every domain that legitimately means this company. The identity guard checks a resolved route against this list, because an ATS board slug is not proof of who owns it.

source.description: Adapter id: greenhouse, lever, ashby, hn, linkedin, manual.

posted_comp.description: Read off the posting by the adapter that fetched it. A field the posting did not state stays null; it never becomes a guess.

sent_at_source.description: Only a transport (SMTP response, ATS confirmation) may stamp this. A client clock produced a whole sweep of CEST times labelled Z.

receipt.description: Path under outputs/receipts/<id>/, copied there by gate record.

notes.description: Free prose lives here and only here.

entry.description: One dated observation. Three arrays instead of one prose blob, because the record that motivated this held 4,000 characters of correction, rewrite history, a declined request and an operational warning in a single notes string.
